assertions_contracts.best_practice: Spec supports compile-time assumption checks on constant expressions and requires-style language extensions; contract-first documentation remains valid
assertions_contracts.evidence: Spot-checked live in this pass: the current WGSL TR still states statements can check assumptions at shader creation time on constant expressions, and the guide text is unchanged on this aspect since run 1 held it
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Contracts per shader (inputs, bindings, backends, fallback) plus requires directives as machine-checked documentation

bounded_work.best_practice: Still sound and uncontradicted; spec loop and override semantics unchanged in ways that affect this
bounded_work.evidence: No contradiction in the current TR fetched in this pass; guide text unchanged since run 1 held it
bounded_work.guide_position: Named constants with units, guarded divisions, statically determinable or constant-bounded loops, per-pixel ALU/texture budgets

concurrency.best_practice: Spec formalises subgroups, subgroup_id, subgroup_size_control and quad operations as named language extensions with uniformity scopes (subgroup_uniformity), so guidance should be extension-gated and specific, not a blanket avoidance
concurrency.evidence: Fix verified present in the current guide text (references/TIGER_STYLE_WGSL.md section 8, and the reworded house-policy bullet in section 9). Live spot-check of the TR in this pass confirms the mechanism the fix cites: the TR's extension table states subgroup_uniformity 'adds an additional scope, subgroup, for uniform control flow' and that subgroup/quad builtins require the subgroups extension, and subgroup_uniformity diagnostics are defined for subgroup and quad builtins
concurrency.guide_position: REMEDIATED (pass 2, item 17): uniformity discipline for derivative/texture ops, plus extension-gated subgroup guidance in section 8 - subgroups, subgroup_id, subgroup_size_control and quad operations may be used on compute-capable targets behind the enable directive plus the section 9 host feature check, with subgroup_uniformity obligations stated; the section 9 portable subset stays subgroup-free as labelled house policy, not a language limit

error_handling.best_practice: Spec still defines shader-creation and pipeline-creation errors as the failure surface; application-side fallback remains the correct host pattern
error_handling.evidence: WGSL TR defines creation-error behaviour and, for subgroups, pipeline-creation errors for override expressions; guide text unchanged since run 1 held it
error_handling.guide_position: Shader-creation error -> log, fall back to a safe material, never black screen silently; requires/enable documented per shader

formatting.best_practice: wgslfmt is the formatter shipped with the wgsl-analyzer project; it formats WGSL and WESL, is actively maintained, and exposes indent controls (--indent-width, --tabs), so a house 4-space / no-tabs rule is expressible with the current tool
formatting.evidence: Run 1 left this unverified for lack of a primary source. Verified in this pass from the tool's own repository: crates/wgslfmt/README.md in wgsl-analyzer/wgsl-analyzer (updated Oct 2026) describes wgslfmt as a tool for formatting WGSL and WESL shader code, installed via cargo from that repo, with --indent-width and --tabs options - the guide's pairing is current, not orphaned
formatting.guide_position: Format with wgslfmt; 4 spaces, no tabs

memory_ownership.best_practice: Does not apply: WGSL has address spaces and host-owned resources, no in-shader ownership/lifetimes
memory_ownership.evidence: Aspect does not apply to a shader language; nearest analogue (bindings/layout) is covered in the guide. Unchanged from run 1
memory_ownership.guide_position: No ownership; guide covers address spaces, binding-slot ownership by the engine, and uniform/storage layout instead

security.best_practice: WGSL remains a sandboxed, statically typed shader language with creation-time validation; guide's defence-in-depth (feature check + fallback) matches the spec model
security.evidence: Live TR spot-check in this pass reconfirms WGSL is statically typed with very limited implicit conversions and creation-time checks; guide text unchanged since run 1 held it
security.guide_position: Portability-as-safety, no f64, feature checks before enable directives, fallback material defined before writing the shader

static_analysis.best_practice: Naga ships versioned inside wgpu (27.x/30.x lines), so the validator version must be pinned to the wgpu/Bevy in use - which is what the remediated record now does; WESL tooling (wesl-rs 0.6.0) is now an alternative front end (see proposals, carried forward)
static_analysis.evidence: Fix verified present in the current guide text (references/TIGER_STYLE_WGSL.md section 15). The recorded version matches current registry state: wgpu 30.0.1 is a current published line and wesl-rs v0.6.0 is the current WESL release
static_analysis.guide_position: REMEDIATED (pass 1 mechanical fix, re-verified pass 2): validate with naga CLI (imports stripped), wgsl-analyzer diagnostics, portability test, screenshot; the section 15 validation record now reads 'naga 30.0.1 (via wgpu 30.0.1): 4 shaders validated (glow, pulse, atmosphere, wipe)' - the run-1 'naga 0.x' pin is gone
